title: DR1 lets a trader copy an address they have already given into a second party role in one click; the frontend tells them the roles are usually the same and makes them pick again.

finding.frontend: The hub row for every party offers exactly one action, an Add or Change link to that party's picker (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:37-46). The importer hint already tells the trader the answer: "This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:32). So the frontend states the shortcut in prose and then makes the trader open the picker, search the book again and re-select the record they have just selected. Nothing named `sameAs` exists anywhere under the addresses or contact features.
finding.prototype: Three of DR1's six sections carry a copy shortcut, rendered as a submit button styled as a link beside the normal Add link and shown only while that section is still empty (app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:83-101). Consignor offers "Same as place of origin" (:91) and importer and place of destination both offer "Same as consignee" (:99); the flags that switch them on are `canUseSameAsPlaceOfOrigin` on consignor and `canUseSameAsConsignee` on importer and place of destination (app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:27,54,68). Pressing one copies the source party's record id, name, address lines and country into the target section and re-renders the hub with that section answered.
finding.difference: Add a copy action to the hub for the three sections DR1 names, shown only while the target section is empty and the source section is answered: "Same as place of origin" on consignor, "Same as consignee" on importer and on place of destination. The hub is already a POST form (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/template.njk:13-17), and a party answer is now an address-book reference rather than a copied block, so the action writes the source party's `addressId` into the target — no address data is duplicated. This depends on the hub sections finding only for where the button sits, not for whether it works.
finding.falsifiedBy: A copy-from-another-party action of any kind appearing on the frontend hub or in either picker.
finding.correction: Verified, no change, and the medium confidence is earned. The shortcut appears in neither captured hub, and the reason is now established rather than assumed: DR1 renders it only in the branch that runs when a section is empty, so the empty hub does not show it because no source party is answered yet, and the answered hub does not show it because every section is already filled. It is real in the source — the three flags sit on consignor, importer and place of destination exactly as the finding says, and the branch renders one or two link-styled submit buttons beside the normal Add link. The frontend side is observable: every hub row carries exactly one action, and no `sameAs` control exists anywhere under the addresses or contact features. One citation is a line early — the importer hint the finding quotes is at copy.en.js:31, not :32. So this is a reading of two sources rather than a comparison of two pictures, which is what medium is for, and it should stay medium unless a capture is taken with one section answered and its dependant empty.

relatedTo.why: both change the same per-section block on the hub
